chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yaq'ub, from 'Allan al-Kulayni, that he ascribed to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that he said: "The sword of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was only named Dhu'l-Faqar because at its center there was a line going along its length similar to the dorsal vertebrae, so it was named Dhu'l-Faqar for that. It was a sword with which Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended from Heaven, and its ring was of silver, and it was he who cried about it from Heaven: 'There is no sword but Dhu'l-Faqar, and there is no hero but Ali.'"

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Believers), a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.ذُو الْفَقَارِ: Dhu'l-Faqar (Possessor of the Two Edges/Vertebrae), the name of Imam Ali's sword

ai.seo_question: Why is Imam Ali's sword called Dhu'l-Faqar and what is its spiritual significance?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* elucidates the etymology of 'Dhu'l-Faqar' by describing a central ridge on the blade resembling the vertebrae of a spine, while also affirming its celestial origin via the Angel Jibra'il. It highlights the unique status of Imam Ali (AS) through the famous heavenly proclamation, a tradition widely cited in Shia scholarship to demonstrate his singular leadership (Imamah) and martial prowess among the companions.
